import { useMutation, useQuery, useQueryClient } from "@tanstack/react-query";
import { toast } from "sonner";
import { API_URL, fetchWithTimeout, getPathScope, throwIfNotOk } from "./core";

export interface ConnectedClientItem {
	id: string;
	kind: "mcp" | "messaging";
	title?: string | null;
	registrationGroupKey?: string | null;
	identifier?: string | null;
	platform?: string | null;
	assignedAgentId?: string | null;
	assignedAgentName?: string | null;
	status: string;
	authState: string;
	lastSeenAt?: number | null;
	userAgent?: string | null;
	capabilities?: Record<string, unknown> | null;
	externalUrl?: string | null;
	linkedUserName?: string | null;
	linkedUserEmail?: string | null;
	/**
	 * The process driving the connection, when it differs from the app that
	 * registered — an Owletto Mac build driven by the Claude Code SDK reports
	 * `claude-code`. `title` is the registered identity; this disambiguates
	 * two apps riding the same runtime.
	 */
	drivenBy?: string | null;
	details?: Record<string, unknown> | null;
}

function clientsUrl(orgSlug: string, path = "", params?: URLSearchParams) {
	const base = `${API_URL}/api/${orgSlug}/clients${path}`;
	const qs = params?.toString();
	return qs ? `${base}?${qs}` : base;
}

export function useConnectedClients(
	agentId?: string | null,
	options?: { enabled?: boolean; refetchInterval?: number },
) {
	const { slug } = getPathScope();

	return useQuery({
		queryKey: ["connected-clients", slug, agentId ?? null],
		queryFn: async (): Promise<ConnectedClientItem[]> => {
			if (!slug) throw new Error("Workspace required");
			const params = new URLSearchParams();
			if (agentId) params.set("agentId", agentId);

			const res = await fetchWithTimeout(clientsUrl(slug, "", params), {
				credentials: "include",
			});
			await throwIfNotOk(res, "Failed to load connected clients");
			const data = (await res.json()) as { clients?: ConnectedClientItem[] };
			return data.clients ?? [];
		},
		enabled: !!slug && (options?.enabled ?? true),
		staleTime: 15_000,
		refetchInterval: options?.refetchInterval,
	});
}

export function useRevokeMcpClient() {
	const { slug } = getPathScope();
	const queryClient = useQueryClient();

	return useMutation({
		mutationFn: async (vars: { clientId: string; scope?: "all" }) => {
			if (!slug) throw new Error("Workspace required");
			const params = new URLSearchParams();
			if (vars.scope === "all") params.set("scope", "all");

			const res = await fetchWithTimeout(
				clientsUrl(slug, `/mcp/${encodeURIComponent(vars.clientId)}`, params),
				{ method: "DELETE", credentials: "include" },
			);
			await throwIfNotOk(res, "Failed to revoke client");
			return (await res.json()) as { revokedClientIds?: string[] };
		},
		onSuccess: () => {
			queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ["connected-clients", slug] });
			toast.success("App access revoked");
		},
		onError: (error: Error) => {
			toast.error(error.message || "Failed to revoke app access");
		},
	});
}
import type { ConnectedClientItem } from "@/lib/api/clients";

/**
 * Connected MCP clients as connectors-list rows.
 *
 * A client is the one INBOUND thing on that list: ChatGPT calling in with a
 * person's access, rather than something an agent reaches out to. It earns a
 * place there because the page is the workspace's connection inventory and
 * revoking a grant belongs with it. It carries no facets — "what can this do
 * for my agents", the axis every chip filters on, is the wrong question to ask
 * of an inbound grant — so it appears only under "All", and only while the
 * grant is live. Expired and revoked registrations stay on the MCP client
 * page, which is the one surface that shows a client's whole history.
 *
 * Clients also surface in Recent, which answers the different question of what
 * has been active lately. That row opens Activity filtered to every
 * registration in the group; the inventory row opens client detail for access
 * management.
 */

/**
 * One row per app, not per registration.
 *
 * A client that re-registers gets a new `oauth_clients` row under the same
 * name, so listing raw registrations shows the same app several times and
 * makes Revoke ambiguous about what it disconnects. The group key comes from
 * the SERVER (`registrationGroupKey` = client_name + owner + org) rather than
 * being re-derived here, so what the UI collapses is exactly what
 * `?scope=all` revokes.
 */
export interface ClientGroup {
	key: string;
	/** Routable id — the group's primary client. Stable and URL-safe. */
	clientId: string;
	title: string;
	/** The process driving the connection, when it differs from the app. */
	drivenBy: string | null;
	clientIds: string[];
	connected: boolean;
	lastSeenAt: number | null;
	linkedUser: string | null;
}

export function groupClients(clients: ConnectedClientItem[]): ClientGroup[] {
	const groups = new Map<string, ClientGroup>();

	for (const client of clients) {
		if (client.kind !== "mcp") continue;

		const title = client.title?.trim() || client.identifier || "Unknown app";
		const key = client.registrationGroupKey || client.id;

		const existing = groups.get(key);
		if (!existing) {
			groups.set(key, {
				key,
				clientId: client.id,
				title,
				drivenBy: client.drivenBy?.trim() || null,
				clientIds: [client.id],
				connected: client.status === "connected",
				lastSeenAt: client.lastSeenAt ?? null,
				linkedUser: client.linkedUserName ?? client.linkedUserEmail ?? null,
			});
			continue;
		}

		existing.clientIds.push(client.id);
		existing.connected = existing.connected || client.status === "connected";
		if ((client.lastSeenAt ?? 0) > (existing.lastSeenAt ?? 0)) {
			existing.lastSeenAt = client.lastSeenAt ?? null;
			// The freshest registration also supplies the driver worth showing.
			existing.drivenBy = client.drivenBy?.trim() || null;
		}
	}

	return [...groups.values()].sort(
		(a, b) => (b.lastSeenAt ?? 0) - (a.lastSeenAt ?? 0),
	);
}

export function relativeTime(ms: number | null): string {
	if (!ms) return "never";
	const diff = Date.now() - ms;
	if (diff < 60_000) return "just now";
	const mins = Math.floor(diff / 60_000);
	if (mins < 60) return `${mins}m ago`;
	const hours = Math.floor(mins / 60);
	if (hours < 24) return `${hours}h ago`;
	return `${Math.floor(hours / 24)}d ago`;
}

/** The row's secondary line: who granted it, and whether it is still live. */
export function clientRowMeta(group: ClientGroup): string {
	const parts = [group.linkedUser];
	parts.push(
		group.connected
			? `active ${relativeTime(group.lastSeenAt)}`
			: "disconnected",
	);
	// "driven by claude-code" is the honest disambiguator when two different
	// apps ride the same runtime — without it the list showed two rows both
	// titled claude-code and Revoke was unattributable.
	if (group.drivenBy && group.drivenBy !== group.title) {
		parts.push(`via ${group.drivenBy}`);
	}
	return parts.filter(Boolean).join(" · ");
}

Pre-review fixer pass complete. The branch (client activity attribution: link MCP clients to their granting member entity, surface client IDs on the detail page and the Activity drill banner) was in good shape — one slop class found and fixed, everything verified green.

**Fixed**
- `linkedUserEntityId` removed end-to-end — it was plumbed through the server response (`client-routes.ts`), the server test, `ConnectedClientItem`, `ClientGroup`/`groupClients`, and the owletto test fixture, but had zero consumers: every link is built from `linkedUserEntitySlug` alone. Since the field was born on this branch, trimming it is scope reduction, not an API break. The server's member-entity lookup simplified from a `Map<string, {id, slug}>` to a `Map<string, string>` and the SQL no longer selects `e.id`.
- `drill-filter-banner.tsx` — missing trailing newline at EOF (was already fixed in the working tree diff; `git diff --check` is clean in both repos).

**Verified (not just compiled)**
- Server query filters (`namespace='auth_user_id'`, `source_connector='auth:signup'`, `et.slug='$member'`) match exactly what `ensureMemberEntity` writes (`member-entity.ts:137-139`), and the org-scoped unique index guarantees at most one row per user.
- `groupClients` merge path can't drop the linkage: `registrationGroupKey` includes `owner_user_id`, so every registration in a group shares the same member.
- The `/$owner/connectors/client/$clientId` route used by `clientSourceLink` exists; the `as "/"` Link cast matches the established pattern (10 existing uses).
- Ran: server `client-routes-identity.test.ts` (4 pass, real DB), owletto `events-tab.test.tsx` (10 pass), `client-rows.test.ts` (10 pass), `tsc --noEmit` clean in both owletto and server.

**Needs the driving agent**
- Nothing to regenerate. `make pre-pr` still owed as the full gate; the owletto submodule commit + pin bump is the driving agent's job.

**Not fixed (judgment call, flagging)**
- `client-detail.tsx` "Registrations" count row is now redundant — the new "Client IDs" row lists every id right above it, so the count is derivable. Removing it is a visible UI choice beyond attribution, so I left it; the reviewer may nit it.
- "Granted by" link markup is duplicated between `client-detail.tsx` and `ClientFilterDetails` (both build `memberUrl` + `<Link>`). Two small call sites with different styling — extracting a shared component felt like premature abstraction, left as is.

**Residual risk**
- The events-tab banner assertions run against MSW-mocked responses; the full browser path (real `/lobu/clients` → drill banner → member page) hasn't been exercised end-to-end in this pass.

# Browser-driven verification (authenticated)

For any UI verification that needs a signed-in session (past the auth wall), use the `agent-browser` CLI with a session cookie minted from the DB. The user's regular Chrome doesn't expose a remote-debug port, so `--auto-connect` will land on the wrong tab — mint a cookie instead.

## Scope

The forged session cookie authenticates the **web admin REST mounted at `/`** (`/api/auth/*`, `/api/<orgSlug>/...`, the SPA — anything `lobu apply` and the web app talk to). It does **NOT** authenticate the **public Agent API at `/lobu`** (`/lobu/api/v1/agents/*`, `/lobu/api/v1/agents/<id>/sessions`) — that path expects a JWT bearer from the OAuth device flow (`lobu login`) or a PAT. If `/lobu/api/v1/agents` returns `401` despite a valid cookie, switch to `lobu chat` / `lobu token`.

## Pick a target

Local dev backend (with prod DB attached over Tailscale): `https://<your-tailscale-host>.ts.net:8443`. Prod: `https://app.lobu.ai`.

## Grab the secret + session token

```bash
# Local dev backend uses .env's BETTER_AUTH_SECRET
SECRET=$(grep '^BETTER_AUTH_SECRET=' .env | cut -d= -f2-)

# Prod uses the secret on the K8s pod
SECRET=$(kubectl exec -n summaries-prod \
  $(kubectl get pod -n summaries-prod -l app.kubernetes.io/name=lobu-app -o name | head -1 | sed 's|pod/||') \
  -- printenv BETTER_AUTH_SECRET)

# Session token from the DB (prod DB serves both targets)
DB="$(grep '^DATABASE_URL=' .env | cut -d= -f2-)"
TOKEN=$(psql "$DB" -tAc "SELECT token FROM session WHERE \"userId\" = '<user_id>' AND \"expiresAt\" > NOW() ORDER BY \"updatedAt\" DESC LIMIT 1")
```

## Sign the cookie

better-auth uses HMAC-SHA256, base64, then URL-encode — base64**url** does *not* validate.

```bash
SIGNED=$(SECRET="$SECRET" TOKEN="$TOKEN" node -e '
  const {createHmac}=require("node:crypto");
  const sig=createHmac("sha256",process.env.SECRET).update(process.env.TOKEN).digest("base64");
  console.log(encodeURIComponent(`${process.env.TOKEN}.${sig}`));
')
```

Cookie name is `__Secure-better-auth.session_token` whenever the baseURL is `https://` (prod and Tailscale dev qualify; only plain-http localhost uses the unprefixed `better-auth.session_token`).

## Drive the browser

```bash
agent-browser --session lobu-verify open "https://app.lobu.ai/"
agent-browser --session lobu-verify eval "document.cookie='__Secure-better-auth.session_token=$SIGNED; path=/; secure; samesite=lax'"
agent-browser --session lobu-verify open "https://app.lobu.ai/<path>"
agent-browser --session lobu-verify wait --text "<expected text>" --timeout 25000
agent-browser --session lobu-verify snapshot -i      # find @refs
agent-browser --session lobu-verify click @e13        # interact
agent-browser --session lobu-verify screenshot --full /tmp/out.png
agent-browser --session lobu-verify close
```

## Driving the paired Owletto extension (connector debugging)

The cookie-forging above and `claude-in-chrome` both drive a *separate* browser that lacks the user's real logged-in sessions — Revolut, for instance, redirects them to `sso.revolut.com/signin`. To run JS or browser actions in the **paired Owletto extension** (the Chrome that holds the user's live sessions, which is what extension-scrape connectors like Revolut/LinkedIn use), go through the connector-operations bridge instead. No deploy required.

`lobu connector run` is the wrong tool here — it only does local Playwright/CDP against a `browser_session` auth profile, so it errors `Missing --auth-profile` for device-worker connectors (Revolut has no auth profile).

For one-off actions, the `lobu call` CLI is the quickest path (usually org `buremba`; connection id from `lobu call manage_connections --org buremba --arg action=list --raw`):

```bash
lobu call manage_operations --org buremba --arg action=execute \
  --arg connection_id=<chrome-connection-id> --arg operation_key=navigate \
  --arg input:='{"url":"https://app.slack.com/...","wait_for_load":true,"open_in_new_tab":true}' --raw
```

For multi-step scripts, use the SDK `operations` namespace via `lobu memory exec` / `run_sdk`:

```js
// chrome connection id: client.connections.list() → connector_key 'chrome'
const ops = await client.operations.listAvailable({ connection_id: CHROME_CONN_ID });
// navigate opens a fresh background tab in the paired Chrome and returns tab_id
const nav = await client.operations.execute({
  connection_id: CHROME_CONN_ID, operation_key: 'navigate',
  input: { url: 'https://app.revolut.com/transactions', open_in_new_tab: true, wait_for_load: true },
});
// evaluate runs arbitrary JS on that tab and returns the JSON-serialised result
await client.operations.execute({
  connection_id: CHROME_CONN_ID, operation_key: 'evaluate',
  input: { tab_id: nav.output.tab_id, expression: '(async()=>{ /* read DOM */ return out })()', await_promise: true },
});
```

`operations.execute` → `dispatchChromeActionToExtension` (`worker-api/dispatch-chrome-action.ts`) → device-worker queue → the paired extension — the same bridge the office-bot Deliveroo connector uses. Chrome ops: `navigate`, `evaluate`, `get_accessibility_tree`, `wait_for_selector`, `click_ref`, `type_ref`, `screenshot`, `show_notification`, `network_intercept_*`, `close_tab`.

Gotchas:
- `search_sdk operations` surfaces the `operations` namespace and current method signatures. Use `Object.keys(client)` inside a `run_sdk` script only when checking discovery/runtime parity.
- Sessions that re-auth often (Revolut, ~hourly) must be freshly logged in *in the paired Chrome* right before you navigate+evaluate, or the fresh tab redirects to the sign-in wall.
- Per-call dispatch latency is 5–60s and virtualized lists recycle content out — for paginated scrapes, iterate inside the connector's own run, not via one-shot `evaluate`s.
- **Connector-side changes ship via re-apply, not the app release.** Per-org connectors (`examples/personal-agent`) live in `connector_definitions`/`connector_versions` and only update on `lobu apply` (or `connections.installConnector` for a single bundle). An app deploy that adds a *capability* (e.g. `show_notification`) does nothing until the connector that *calls* it is re-applied. **And a new chrome action also needs the matching handler in the extension build** — dispatching `show_notification` to an older installed extension fails with `Owletto for Chrome: unknown dispatch ... action_key='show_notification'`. So three things gate such a notification: an up-to-date extension build (the handler), a re-applied connector (the call), and macOS notification permission on the extension.

payload.input:
const r = await tools.exec_command({cmd:"set -euo pipefail
LOBUBROWSER_APP_POD=$(kubectl get pod -n summaries-prod -l app.kubernetes.io/component=api -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}')
LOBUBROWSER_SECRET=$(kubectl exec -n summaries-prod "$LOBUBROWSER_APP_POD" -- printenv BETTER_AUTH_SECRET)
LOBUBROWSER_USER=$(kubectl exec -n summaries-prod lobu-ai-prod-db-1 -- psql -U postgres -d owletto -tAc "SELECT user_id FROM oauth_tokens WHERE client_id = 'REDACTED' ORDER BY (revoked_at IS NULL AND expires_at > NOW()) DESC, created_at DESC LIMIT 1" 2>/dev/null)
LOBUBROWSER_TOKEN=$(kubectl exec -n summaries-prod lobu-ai-prod-db-1 -- psql -U postgres -d owletto -tAc "SELECT token FROM session WHERE \"userId\" = '$LOBUBROWSER_USER' AND \"expiresAt\" > NOW() ORDER BY \"updatedAt\" DESC LIMIT 1" 2>/dev/null)
LOBUBROWSER_SIGNED=$(LOBUBROWSER_SECRET="$LOBUBROWSER_SECRET" LOBUBROWSER_TOKEN="$LOBUBROWSER_TOKEN" node -e 'const {createHmac}=require("node:crypto"); const sig=createHmac("sha256",process.env.LOBUBROWSER_SECRET).update(process.env.LOBUBROWSER_TOKEN).digest("base64"); process.stdout.write(encodeURIComponent(`${process.env.LOBUBROWSER_TOKEN}.${sig}`));')
agent-browser --session client-attribution-click-live open 'https://buremba.lobu.ai/' >/dev/null
agent-browser --session client-attribution-click-live eval "document.cookie='__Secure-better-auth.session_token=$LOBUBROWSER_SIGNED; path=/; secure; samesite=lax'; void 0" >/dev/null
agent-browser --session client-attribution-click-live open 'https://buremba.lobu.ai/activity?REDACTED' >/dev/null
agent-browser --session client-attribution-click-live wait --text 'Granted by' --timeout 25000 >/dev/null
agent-browser --session client-attribution-click-live screenshot /tmp/client-activity-attribution-live.png
agent-browser --session client-attribution-click-live snapshot -i | rg 'From ChatGPT|Burak Emre Kabakcı'","workdir":"/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/client-activity-attribution","yield_time_ms":30000,"max_output_tokens":5000}); text(r.output)
